verdict.rationale: Unity's own docs confirm it canceled the controversial per-install Runtime Fee (unity-docs-21), and Personal/Pro tiers are seat/subscription-based rather than royalty-based (unity-docs-15/31). However, community evidence directly contradicts the 'keep what you earn, no surprise fees' framing: HN commenters describe the original per-install fee as 'insane' (unity-comm-1), report Unity unilaterally forcing a customer into a pricier license and doubling costs 'just because they can' (unity-comm-5), and describe reputational damage with users 'planning to switch engines' (unity-comm-11). This is a concrete, documented case of the licensing model behaving less permissively than vendor messaging implies, not just general skepticism. Missing for 10: current post-cancellation royalty terms confirmed independently, and resolution/rebuttal of the forced-upgrade complaints.
